questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Lesotho?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Lesotho article.

questions.proof: The capital of Lesotho is Maseru.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Lesotho?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Lesotho on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Lesotho article.

questions.proof: Lesotho's position is unusual: it is completely surrounded by South Africa and has no borders with any other country.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Lesotho became a country in _____, but it was then called Basutoland.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the nineteenth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Lesotho article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: Lesotho became a country in 1818, but it was then called Basutoland.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Lesotho eventually gained its independence on 4 October _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Lesotho article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: Lesotho eventually gained its independence on 4 October 1966.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “This new country came under attack from its enemies and in _____ Moshoeshoe asked Queen Victoria of Great Britain for help.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the nineteenth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Lesotho article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: This new country came under attack from its enemies and in 1868 Moshoeshoe asked Queen Victoria of Great Britain for help.
